body.statement: The ATE identified set over the closed class \(\mathcal M(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\) is exactly \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{com}}=[L,R]\), with \(L\) and \(R\) defined by one common \((w_{0,x},w_{1,x})\in D_{A,x}\) per stratum.  Every endpoint is attained by a law in \(\mathcal M\): at an interior selected pair the law uses the selected feasible risks as conditional Bernoulli marginals and any coupling of \((Y(0),Y(1))\) given \((X,U)\), while a boundary selected pair is attained as the finite-simplex limit of such strictly positive laws.  Over \(\mathcal M^{\circ}\), \(\inf\tau=L\), \(\sup\tau=R\), and the closure of the identified set is \([L,R]\); endpoint attainment is asserted there only when an attaining law is itself strictly positive.  When \((w_{0,x},w_{1,x},\theta_{0,x},\theta_{1,x})\) is fixed in the interior chart, the formula reduces exactly to the Rosenbaum--Rubin Section 4 recalculation.
body.justification: This is the sharp population kernel: both potential-outcome arms must be simultaneously realizable through the same latent confounder.
body.gap: Rosenbaum--Rubin evaluate fixed sensitivity tuples; Ciocănea-Teodorescu--Gabriel--Sjölander use distinct exposure-standardization parameters; and Dorn--Guo prove sharpness for a different propensity-only model.  None gives this closed bounded common-binary-\(U\) iff envelope.
body.consumer: Investigators using interpretable binary-confounder calibrations obtain the narrowest logically valid ATE interval rather than an armwise diagnostic envelope.
